title: Achy Eye, Hates the Light

patient.name: Ms Devi d/o Kumar
patient.presenting_complaint: One red eye with deep ache and light sensitivity, no discharge

history.hpc: Ms Devi says 'My left eye got a deep ache and very sensitive to light, but no discharge one. The light really bother me.' One eye, aching pain, marked photophobia, slightly blurred, no sticky discharge.
history.pmhx: History of joint pains being investigated by a rheumatologist. Has had a similar red, light-sensitive eye once before.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left eye red, no discharge; cornea/anterior chamber to be examined by the doctor

investigations.history_and_triage: Focused history shows a painful, markedly photophobic red eye with no discharge and a smaller/normal pupil pattern — features of iritis/uveitis rather than conjunctivitis, with a relevant joint-problem history.
investigations.red_flags_checked: Marked photophobia, deep ache and reduced vision are red flags; the no-discharge pattern argues against simple conjunctivitis.
investigations.triage_category: Urgent — escalate for prompt doctor assessment and possible referral.

diagnosis: A painful, markedly photophobic red eye with no discharge, mildly reduced vision and a history of joint problems fits an iritis/uveitis pattern rather than conjunctivitis. The PSA recognises the red flags, escalates for prompt doctor review, and does not make a medical diagnosis.

immediate: Confirm identity and take a focused red-eye history
Apply the red-eye differential: no discharge + marked photophobia + ache suggests iritis, not conjunctivitis
Ask about relevant systemic history (joint problems) and previous similar episodes
Record visual acuity and escalate for prompt doctor review
follow_up: Doctor assessment with slit lamp; possible referral and treatment
Advise the patient to avoid bright light and return if worse
patient_education: Explain the eye needs to be checked by the doctor promptly
Reassure that light sensitivity is being taken seriously
Advise returning urgently if pain or vision worsens

key_points: Confirms identity and takes a focused red-eye history
Asks about discharge, pain, photophobia and vision
Asks about relevant systemic (joint) history and previous episodes
Applies the red-eye differential and notes the no-discharge, photophobic pattern
Identifies photophobia and ache as red flags
Links the joint history as relevant
Recognises an iritis/uveitis pattern needing prompt review
Does not make a medical diagnosis — escalates
Understands why photophobia + no discharge is concerning
Knows the systemic association is relevant
